capability: Single-phase Darcy flow and Theis drawdown

quantity.name: drawdown transient
quantity.observable: Radial drawdown s(r,t) = p0 - p(r,t) at t = 1000 s, compared pointwise to the Theis closed form over 2 m < r < 60 m. T and Ss are additionally recovered together by a two-parameter fit of s = A E1(B r^2), which gives T = Q/(4 pi A) and Ss = 4 T t B, so the two are identified separately rather than only through their ratio.
quantity.supersedes: The previous row identified only the diffusivity T/Ss and reported the Theis and Cooper-Jacob fits as diagnostic. The residual turned out to be timestep discretization, not identifiability: the Theis solution is steep at early time, and the seed's dt = 200 left a 2.4% bias that falls to 0.2% at dt = 10.

reference.derivation: The shipped seed parameters require a consistent transmissivity/storage reduction before numeric values can be asserted; no plausible number is invented.
reference.confirmed_from: PLAN.md equation and version-matched theis1.i seed

darcy_sanity_contract.source: Independent Darcy units check added during review rework; not used as Theis acceptance value

derived_mapping.derivation: Divide the PorousFlow mass equation by rho0: S=phi/K and T=k/mu for unit thickness; rho0 cancels from both coefficients.

tolerance.rationale: Declared from PLAN.md before solve; result remains PARTIAL until storage/transmissivity mapping is independently confirmed.

convergence.note: The dominant error is temporal, not spatial: at fixed nx the max deviation over the window falls 0.055, 0.028, 0.011 as dt halves.

source_strength.how_established: PorousFlowBasicTHM here runs with multiply_by_density = false, so the PorousFlowSquarePulsePointSource mass_flux enters the volume equation directly. The two candidate readings were tested against the drawdown: taken as volumetric it gives a ratio of 0.997 to the closed form, taken as a mass rate divided by density it is off by a factor of 981. The volumetric reading is the one the code implements.

axisymmetric_case.derivation: Ss = phi/K_f with biot_coefficient = 1 (the solid term (1-alpha)(alpha-phi)/K_s vanishes); T = k/mu for unit thickness; D = T/Ss.

transmissivity_recovery.metric: relative error of the fitted T against k/mu

storage_recovery.metric: relative error of the fitted Ss against phi/K_f

boundary_influence.metric: drawdown at the outer boundary normalized by the drawdown at the inner edge of the fit window
boundary_influence.rationale: The closed form assumes an infinite aquifer; the outer boundary must be far enough out to be undisturbed.
